sanskrit_verse:
कायिका कालिका चैव चक्रवृद्धिरतोऽपरा ।
कारिता च शिखावृद्धिर्भोगलाभस्तथैव च ॥
transliteration: kāyikā kālikā caiva cakravṛddhir ato 'parā / kāritā ca śikhāvṛddhir bhogalābhas tathaiva ca //
sph_interpretive_translation: Physical expansion, temporal augmentation, cyclical increase beyond measure—these arise from executed action and the growth of spiritual discipline, as well as from material acquisition.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from realized capacity, not mere intent
Causation is sequential and manifests through dharma-aligned action
Capacity-based responsibility includes both material and spiritual stewardship
Restoration logic requires alignment with natural and spiritual consequence cycles
Consciousness alignment determines the legitimacy of acquired growth
executable_legal_axioms: IF an entity demonstrates expanded physical or temporal influence THEN verify alignment with dharma-sanctioned causality
IF growth exceeds cyclic norms THEN assess source of action: self-executed, delegated, or induced
IF material gain accompanies spiritual claim THEN validate integrity of śikhāvṛddhi (spiritual discipline)
IF expansion lacks conscious acknowledgment THEN initiate restorative completion protocols
IF causality chain breaks THEN assign responsibility to nearest conscious executor
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating matters involving disproportionate accumulation or expansion, the Supreme Court must evaluate not just legality but the ontological alignment of the actor's consciousness with the causal sequence of dharma-sanctioned action. Responsibility is assigned based on proximity to conscious execution, not passive ownership.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that all forms of increase—physical, temporal, or experiential—are rooted in prior action. This succession (anupūrvaśaḥ) demands recognition rather than punishment. Responsibility is proportional to awareness and enactment, not outcome alone. Justice aligns consciousness with its causal footprint without invoking punitive measures.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate karmic reflection process to restore causal awareness
Assign completion rituals for unacknowledged gains
Realign material and spiritual accumulations with declared dharmic purpose
Facilitate śikhāvṛddhi rectification through guided spiritual discipline
Reintegrate displaced consciousness through voluntary restitution
final_declaration: Thus declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Dharma. Expansion without alignment is incomplete; completion restores order. There is no punishment—only realignment of consciousness with its lawful cause. Dharma is restored.
